Traitana appears in the Rigveda^1 as a Dāsa, an enemy of
Dīrghatamas, who seems to have engaged him in single
combat and defeated him. The St. Petersburg Dictionary
suggests that he is rather a supernatural being allied to Trita
(cf. the Avestan Thrita and Thraetaona).^2
1) i. 158, 5.
2) Macdonell, Vedic Mythology, p. 68.
Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the Rig-
veda, 3, 151; Oldenberg, Religion des
Veda, 144.

Trai-dhātva (‘descendant of Tridhātu,’) is the patronymic
of Tryaruṇa in the Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa (xiii. 3, 12).

Trai-pada, neut., occurs as a measure of distance, ‘three-
quarters’ of a Yojana, in the Pañcāviṃśa Brāhmaṇa, where
half a Yojana is termed Gavyūti and a quarter Krośa.^1
1) xvi. 13. Cf. Śāṅkhāyana Śrauta Sūtra, xiv. 41, 12.

Traivaṇi is mentioned as a pupil of Aupacandhani or Aupa-
jandhani in the first two Vaṃśas (lists of teachers) in the
Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad.^1 In the Mādhyaṃdina recension^2

Trai-vṛṣṇa, ‘descendant of Trivṛṣan,’ is the patronymic of
Trayaruṇa in the Rigveda (v. 27, 1).
